opportunities.title: Youth Hub: Cricut Waterbottles (2 Part)
opportunities.description: Learn how to use the Cricut to create and cut custom vinyl designs to personalize your waterbottle. Please note this is a 2 day program. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more. If you identify as a person with a disability or as a person who is Deaf, and require an accessibility accommodation to participate in this program, please contact Accessibility Services by email accessibleservices@tpl.ca , or voicemail, 416-393-7099, to make a request. Please contact us at least three weeks in advance.

opportunities.title: Excel Basics 2: Do More with your Data
opportunities.description: An introductory class on Microsoft Excel for beginners with little or no Excel experience. Build on your basic Microsoft Excel skills and learn to use Excel data effectively. In this second session, you will: Practice data entry and formatting Manipulate rows and columns Create and copy simple formulas Convert data to a Table then sort and filter Create your first chart Upon completion of this class, you will be able to get more from your data using tables, filters and charts. Prerequisites: Excel Basics Part 1 or equivalent knowledge. Basic mouse and keyboard skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. opportunities.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ 3D printer. Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software. Registration is required via tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: Drop in anytime between 3-4 PM for a fun-filled hour of STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Math) exploration! Registration begins August 30 Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners
opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Prerequisites: No computer experience required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this second session you will: Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys) Practice proper keyboarding posture Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice. Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 or basic mouse skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Computers for Beginners 3: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment. Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Computers for Beginners 4: Use the Internet An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Computers for Beginners 5: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Prerequisites: Computers for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse, keyboarding and internet skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Computers for Beginners 6: Use Gmail Learn to use Gmail, Google’s free web-based email service. In this sixth session you will: Practice basic email functions: send, read, reply, forward, delete email, and attach files Review how spam and junk mail work Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to use email. Instructions on how to set up and manage your own free Gmail account are included in the handout. Prerequisites: Basic keyboarding and mouse skills required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Snap Circuits
opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Join an After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! After School Clubs are offered for children ages 6-12 at select branches. Activities can include make and take projects, coding and robotics workshops and more! Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. After School Club: Snap Circuits Play with electricity and circuitry during this hand-on program! Turn on a light, spin a motor, activate a speaker and choose from hundreds of different projects. Or try making your own circuits! No registration required

opportunities.title: STEMWorks Circuit Building Workshop
opportunities.description: Participants will work in groups to build electrical circuits based on provided wiring diagrams. They will start with simple components such as LEDs, motors, and resistors, and gradually progress to more complex circuits involving sensors, wireless control, and LCD displays. This program is only for children aged 9 to 12 years. Registration is required. Please only register the children that will be participating, accompanying adults do not need to register. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6-12. Program supplies are all provided. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. Monday September 14: Button-Making - Come make some buttons at the library to decorate your bag for back to school! Monday September 21: LEGO Building - Build something new with LEGO while making new friends! Monday September 28: Crochet - Learn the basics of how to crochet! For complete beginners. Accessibility Live or automated closed captioning, sign language interpretation, intervenor services, or attendant services are available upon request. Please submit your request at least 2 weeks in advance to: tpl.ca/accessibility-events .

opportunities.title: What the Heck is Roblox? Kids, KidTech and Digital Play
opportunities.description: Anna Hudson, Graduate Program in Art History, Department of Visual Art & Art History, School of the Arts, Media, Performance & Design This talk will focus on how visual arts serves as a bridge, a touchstone, a talking point between people from all walks of life and backgrounds . Bringing people together to communicate and understand different life experiences and ideas is what a curator can encourage. But the flip side of this coin is the reality of the art world. What art does the general public get to see and why? This presentation will also talk about art museums, collectors and the art market as a global phenomenon.

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Introduction to the Makerspace (with a Glowforge Laser Engraver Demo & Group Activity) *** Pls note that this session is generally geared towards older children and adults. Extra colouring sheets & activities are available for younger children. *** PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: (九月專題：新學期，新起點！新移民家庭的「開學收心指南」) Back-to-School Reset – Building Healthy Routines and Digital Habits
opportunities.description: Join Family Services York Region for a practical Back-to-School Reset! This session is facilitated in Mandarin and is perfect for newcomer families. Gain tools for smoother transitions and balanced tech use. Participants will learn: How to establish healthy family routines. How to manage screen time. How to build positive digital habits that support your child’s success in schools. 開學了，如何幫助孩子收心？ 總是為了手機、電腦和孩子吵架？ 誠邀您參加 「 開學收心指南」實用講座！ 一起解鎖健康家庭作息、合理控管螢幕時間，培養健康的電子產品使用習慣。 *The program's facilitator also speaks Cantonese*

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Passive Worksheets (Wordsearches & Colouring) + Kapla Blocks & Challenge Cards + Guest Speaker Day speaker from City of Markham's Environmental Services, 11am-12 noon PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. At the end of the session you will receive a quick tour of Markham Village's sound booth and more information on how to book the space. With your new skills, why not participate in our upcoming Markham Village Film Festival ? Hope to see you there. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!

opportunities.title: Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI
opportunities.description: Learn how to preserve your memories by converting 35mm slides or negatives into high resolution digital images. This demonstration introduces the process of scanning 35mm slides, and AI-powered restoration/modification techniques to remove deterioration and correcting the images' colours. Participants will leave with the knowledge needed to begin digitizing and restoring their own slide collections. Learning outcomes: Learn how to scan and digitize 35mm slides (or negatives) using Makerspace equipment Use AI tools to enhance scanned images by correcting colour and removing common imperfections Note: Program may allow drop-in participants, if space allows. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified! Check out the other Digital Innovation Month Tours and Programs - all happening this month: Markham Village: Tour Demo - Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity Thornhill Community Centre Tour Demo - Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI Aaniin Tour Workshop - Cricut - Make an MPL Canvas Tote Bag Angus Glen Tour Workshop - How to Laser Engrave a Wooden Magnet with The Glowforge (4/5 - Digital Innovation Month Makerspace Series) Cornell Tour Demo #1 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 11am Demo #2 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 3pm

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Thornhill Community Centre
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Pixel Art Game Design Workshop
opportunities.description: In this fun, hands-on, creative workshop run by Cuddles Learning , students will create and export their own pixel characters and environments using iPads, while solving creative design challenges and exploring the fundamentals of game design. They’ll learn the basics of grids, palettes, and layers. No prior experience is required - just imagination! Learning outcomes: Develop creative problem-solving skills through game design challenges Learn how visual design supports gameplay and user experience Apply planning, critical thinking, and creativity to complete a digital game-inspired project Please note this program is designed for all ages.

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Discover a Career in Science/Health Care
opportunities.description: Are you interested in starting a career in the field of health care? Or perhaps you work in the health care field and are looking to add to your education to move into a new area of health care? We’ll highlight important things such as: We will cover programs such as Personal Support Worker, Practical Nursing, Registered Nursing and Medical Device Reprocessing We will cover programs in the field of Science We will touch on entrance requirements, steps to apply A bit about financial aid and student supports **Please note: This workshop is run in partnership with Seneca Polytechnic**. _______ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.
